newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stock exchange expects investor incentives.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stock exchange expects investor incentives.

text.p: The Cypriot government is due to announce incentives in the next few days to spur investor activity on the Cyprus stock exchange, its director said on Wednesday.
"The government is looking at some incentives and we hope they will be announced in the next two or three days," director Nondas Metaxas told Reuters.
Cyprus stock exchange expects investor incentives
Shares on the 41-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) general index fell 1.16 percent to a new low of 77.45 on Wednesday after closing at 78.36 on Tuesday, its lowest level in 10 months.
Metaxas declined to elaborate on the nature of the incentives, but said they were not prompted by the recent lows on the exchange.
Other market sources said the government is due to announce measures relating to taxation allowances which will benefit listed companies and investors.

Analysts have said the market decline was prompted in part by renewed tension on the militarily divided island and a gloomy outlook for the economy. But some attributed to a reaction to a heavy buying spree at the start of the week.
"We are not concerned and we expect to see a rise soon," said Metaxas.

He said the exchange has cut the levy charged to brokers from 1.5 pounds per thousand pounds worth of transactions to 1 pound per thousand. The charges were set before the exchange started operating on March 29 1996.
"Now we know we can survive with less income," he said.
